verdict: BD closed its first year as a focused med-tech company with revenue up 5.4% to $5.3B and operating income nearly doubling, as lower product costs and much smaller legal charges lifted the bottom line.

kpis.label: EPS (GAAP)
kpis.note: continuing operations, vs $1.20 a year ago

segments.name: Medical Essentials
segments.note: Everyday hospital consumables — medication delivery (syringes, catheters) and specimen management (blood-collection tubes) — the largest segment, up 5.9% YoY.

segments.name: Connected Care
segments.note: Medication-management systems and advanced patient monitoring — up 1.6%, as 15% growth in patient monitoring offset a 2% dip in medication management.

segments.name: BioPharma Systems
segments.note: Pre-fillable syringes and drug-delivery systems sold to pharmaceutical companies — up 6.5%.

segments.name: Interventional
segments.note: Peripheral intervention, urology and critical care, and surgery products — the fastest-growing segment, up 7.6%.

opex.name: Selling and administrative expense
opex.note: Selling products and running the company — up 4% YoY.

opex.name: Research & development
opex.note: Developing new medical devices — down 7% YoY.

opex.name: Integration, restructuring and transaction expense
opex.note: Costs of combining, restructuring and deal work, including the Life Sciences separation — down from $125M a year ago.

opex.name: Other operating expense, net
opex.note: Mostly product-liability and other legal matters — down sharply from $232M a year ago.

otherDetail: Interest expense of $130M, plus $11M of other expense, partly offset by $10M of interest income — a net $131M cost.
oneTimers: Adjusted EPS of $4.15 excludes $346M of pre-tax purchase-accounting adjustments (mostly amortization from past acquisitions), $42M of integration costs, $35M of restructuring costs and $32M of separation costs tied to the Life Sciences spin-off.
Cost of products sold included a $66M benefit from refunds of tariffs imposed under IEEPA, partly offset in other operating expense by $45M of product-liability and other legal charges.
This page uses continuing operations. Total net income including discontinued operations was $696M ($2.54 per diluted share).

takeaways.title: Growth was broad-based
takeaways.text: All four segments grew. Interventional led at +7.6% to $1.47B, BioPharma Systems rose 6.5% and Medical Essentials 5.9%; only Connected Care was soft, at +1.6%.

takeaways.title: Operating income nearly doubled
takeaways.text: Operating income rose to $1,032M from $536M. Cost of products sold actually fell 2% despite higher sales, and other operating expense dropped from $232M to $76M as last year's legal charges eased.

takeaways.title: Cash flow jumped for the full year
takeaways.text: Fiscal 2026 free cash flow — cash from continuing operations minus capital spending — rose 42.5% to $2.9B, giving the reshaped company room to pay down debt and buy back shares.

footerNote: Segment revenue for Medical Essentials is shown $1M lower ($1,785M vs the reported $1,786M segment total) so the four segments sum exactly to reported revenue of $5,274M; the unit-level figures in the release round the other way. All flow figures are continuing operations.
